transcript.answer: Lore's agents run in pods of the external floor (ADR-049), and Lore holds no Kubernetes client to start them. The floor's own cluster agent runs those pods. The floor installs the ai-agent-subsystem controller itself, in its own namespace. ADR-031's 2026-10-02 amendment removed Lore's own controller (the `ai-agents` subchart), its cluster agent and the satellite chart from the `lore-platform` umbrella. Lore's cluster agent, catalog sync and claim routes still serve the lines still on `apps/floor`, and they go away with it. Before this change, `apps/cluster-agent` was the only process that held a Kubernetes client, and the Floor reached it over HTTP (ADR-024 and ADR-044 amendments).
sources: CLAUDE.md (Architecture: 'Agents run in pods of the external floor (ADR-049); Lore holds no Kubernetes client')

judgements.reason: The answer correctly says the pods run on the external floor and that Lore holds no Kubernetes client, but it omits that Lore reaches the floor only through @re-cinq/floor-client (FLOOR_API_URL), and it muddies the picture by saying Lore's cluster agent still serves some lines.
